passages.name: Section 2.1 — coordinate-pair notation and permutation set
passages.statement_original: For the sake of notation clarity, we define $\mathbf{z}_{i,kl}=(X_{i,k},Y_{i,l})$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, $1\leq k\leq p$ and $1\leq l\leq q$, and $\mathcal P_m$ as the set of all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$.

passages.name: Section 2.1 — indicator contrast psi
passages.statement_original: We further define $\psi(z_1,z_2,z_3)=I(z_2<z_1)-I(z_3<z_1)$, where $I(\cdot)$ is an indicator function,

passages.name: Section 2.1 — four-argument contrast omega
passages.statement_original: and $\omega(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4)=I(z_1\vee z_3<z_2\wedge z_4)+I(z_1\vee z_3>z_2\wedge z_4)-I(z_1\vee z_2<z_3\wedge z_4)-I(z_1\vee z_2>z_3\wedge z_4)$, where $a\vee b=\max(a,b)$ and $a\wedge b=\min(a,b)$.

policy: These unranked local auxiliary definitions remain part of the audited paper artifact. The editorial passage names identify notation; they are not claimed as author-supplied API titles or as library availability verdicts. Their related-theorem IDs are derived through the reviewed local dependencies.

standard_ambient_resolution.notation: Probability, expectation, conditional expectation, variance and covariance
standard_ambient_resolution.resolution: Standard measure-theoretic meanings are assumed by the source. Specialized projection and variance formulas are explicitly archived in D6, D9-D11 and D16-D17.

standard_ambient_resolution.notation: C(n,d), finite permutations and indicator functions
standard_ambient_resolution.resolution: The source combination convention is retained in D2; permutation and indicator helpers are retained in A1-A3 above.

The exact Section 2.1 random-sample and continuous-vector convention is D1. It does not say that the coordinates within a vector are independent. The precise intended meaning of continuous vector is not further defined.
Theorems 1 and 2 explicitly explain their arrow notation; both explanations are preserved in the original statements.
The exact rates and dimension guards are retained in Assumption 1 and (8)-(10). No universal rate restriction on p/n or q/n is inserted.

standard_ambient_resolution.notation: Bivariate Gaussian law, Pearson correlation, arcsine, sine, cosine, infimum and supremum
standard_ambient_resolution.resolution: Standard ambient concepts in Theorem 5. Its M_h functions, integral formulas and extrema are defined in the theorem itself. No rank-statistic independence condition is added to its Gaussian hypothesis.

standard_ambient_resolution.notation: Normal cdf Phi and universal constant C
standard_ambient_resolution.resolution: Theorem 3 explicitly defines Phi and states that C is independent of n, p and q in its continuation on page 10.
Main-text mentions of supplement results are retained for source fidelity. No supplement statement, proof, simulation or algorithm is imported into the census.

unresolved_source_conventions.issue: The printed summation uses non-strict indices while C(n,d) is defined using distinct elements. The word distinctive also describes a pair of coordinate indices drawn from different vector index sets. Preserve the text and formula; do not assume an unprinted k!=l restriction or repair the summation.
The second and fourth comparisons use maximum greater than minimum as printed, and the X-argument list has an extra comma. These are retained instead of substituting a standard four-point kernel.

The source first calls S squared the full aggregate variance, presents a dominating leading-term variance, and says S squared is kernel-independent in an asymptotic sense. Theorem 2 nevertheless states exact unbiasedness. The audit preserves this ambiguity instead of declaring an exact finite-sample equality.

The text uses S-hat in a denominator after defining S-hat squared by a signed unbiased estimate. It does not specify a convention for a negative or zero estimate. The six-index formula also requires enough observations; no unprinted regularization is inserted.

The source specifies p-divergent and q-divergent limits separately, while the theorems require max(p,q) to diverge. Preserve these guards; the source does not require both dimensions to diverge or explicitly specify all nondivergent subsequence conventions.

unresolved_source_conventions.source: Section 2.4 — projection sums and S_h, page 10
unresolved_source_conventions.issue: The M-hat display feeds coordinate-pair arguments to G_h, which is next defined on full observations. The same section relates its own second-projection variance S_h squared to S squared. Preserve the argument notation and local-alternative scale instead of importing the null product variance.

The second coordinate range is printed as 1<=l<=p rather than q. The Gaussian/correlation domain and zero-correlation ratio convention are not further specified; the extrema explicitly exclude rho=0. Preserve the printed statement.
